name: Metabolic syndrome
seoTitle: Metabolic syndrome Calculator: Free, With Steps
seoDesc: Metabolic syndrome: work out blood pressure from the total score. A free health calculator with the formula, units and a worked example.
summary: The Metabolic syndrome calculator is a free, no-sign-up health tool. Fill in the 5 fields it asks for and it works out blood pressure straight away, with the formula shown underneath. That makes it useful for an informed starting point to take to a clinician, not a diagnosis. Nothing is submitted anywhere: the arithmetic runs in the page you are looking at.

sections.title: How does the Metabolic syndrome calculator work?
sections.html:
The Metabolic syndrome calculator takes the values in the form, applies the relationship described below and reports blood pressure in the results panel.

Working from the top of the form: you choose the option that describes your case (the waist circumference, the triglyceride levels and the HDL levels); then you type in the total score.

Press Calculate once and the page holds the relationship, tracking which boxes you filled and working out everything else; from that point on it follows every edit you make.

Because the equation can be rearranged for each of its variables, the page also runs backwards. Leave the box you want to know empty, fill in the rest, and it solves for the missing one instead. That is useful when you know the answer you need rather than the inputs you have.

sections.title: What do you need to enter?
sections.html:
• A single on/off switch — tick it for “women: >35 inches, men: >40 inches”, leave it clear for the other case. It changes which relationship the calculator applies, not just a multiplier.
  • A single on/off switch — tick it for “≥ 150 Mg/d l or on triglyceride lowering prescription”, leave it clear for the other case. It changes which relationship the calculator applies, not just a multiplier.
  • A single on/off switch — tick it for “women: <50 Mg/d l, men: <40 Mg/d l”, leave it clear for the other case. It changes which relationship the calculator applies, not just a multiplier.
  • A single on/off switch — tick it for “>100 Mg/d l or on glucose lowering prescription”, leave it clear for the other case. It changes which relationship the calculator applies, not just a multiplier.
  • A plain number with no unit attached.

5 fields on this form are a choice rather than a number. Those choices decide which version of the calculation applies, so they are worth setting before you worry about the digits.

sections.title: The formula behind the Metabolic syndrome calculator
sections.html:
One relationship drives the whole page:

Blood pressure=-waist circumference − fasting glucose − HDL levels − triglyceride levels + total score

Read it as an ordinary equation. Where a word appears instead of a letter, it is the label of one of the boxes in the form; where a function appears, it is the usual mathematical meaning of that function.

sections.title: What does the result mean?
sections.html:
• The option the calculation settles on.

Before doubting the arithmetic, check the inputs: a unit chip on the wrong setting, a drop-down left at its default, or a percentage typed as a whole number rather than a decimal will each shift the answer by a clean power of ten.

sections.title: When should you use it?
sections.html:
The Metabolic syndrome calculator earns its place in the middle of a task, not instead of one. It is most useful when:

  • Tracking a measurement over time and understanding what changed
  • Deciding whether a reading is worth a second look
  • Preparing for an appointment so you can describe your numbers clearly
  • Any time the same 1 figures keep coming back — the total score — and you would rather not repeat the arithmetic by hand each time.

sections.title: How do you get a reliable answer?
sections.html:
• Write the answer down with its unit. A bare number copied into a report later is exactly where units get lost.
  • Leave the field you want solved for empty rather than guessing at it. Filling every box tells the calculator you already know the answer.
  • Change one input at a time when you are exploring. Two simultaneous changes make it impossible to tell which one moved the result.
  • Keep the units you enter consistent. Mixing centimetres into a field that expects metres is the single most common way to get an answer that is out by a factor of a hundred.

sections.title: What else is worth knowing?
sections.html:
• Filling in more than one box is fine. The most recently edited field is the one treated as known, so you can switch direction without reloading.
  • Answers that depend on a drop-down reflect the option you picked, not a range. Switching to a neighbouring option is the quickest way to see how much that factor matters.
  • Some options are backed by reference tables that ship with the page, so the values are fixed data rather than a live lookup.

sections.title: What are the limits worth knowing?
sections.html:
Every tool draws a boundary somewhere. For the Metabolic syndrome calculator, these are the ones that matter:

  • The 5 drop-downs on this page offer a fixed list of cases. A value that is not on the list cannot be entered, and the nearest option is not always a good substitute.
  • The calculator reports what the relationship implies; it does not judge whether the inputs themselves are sensible, so a figure that is out by a factor of ten will produce an answer that is out by the same factor.

sections.title: How do you check the answer yourself?
sections.html:
• Change one input at a time — waist circumference for instance — and watch which results move. A result that stays put does not depend on it.
  • Try a round value you can work out in your head. If the answer matches your mental arithmetic, the inputs are on the scale you assumed.
  • Re-enter the same figure and confirm the result is stable; a number that moves when you press Calculate again is a sign that a field is still empty.

faq.q: What does the Metabolic syndrome calculator work out?
faq.a: It returns blood pressure, derived from the total score. Every field in the form feeds the same relationship: press Calculate once and changing any of them updates the result immediately, with no page reload.

faq.q: What do I need to enter to use the Metabolic syndrome calculator?
faq.a: The form asks for the total score, which is 5 fields in total. Each one is labelled with what it means and, where relevant, the unit it expects. Anything you leave blank is treated as the value to solve for.
Yes. Each variable in the relationship can be the one being solved for: fill in the answer you are aiming at, leave the field you want empty, and the calculator inverts the equation for you.

faq.q: How much do the drop-down choices change the answer?
faq.a: There are several choices to make (5 in total), and each one selects a different case rather than scaling the result. Switching a single option and watching the result is the fastest way to see how much that choice is worth.

With the values the page starts from, the calculator reports Total score = 0. Treat that as a reference point rather than a recommendation: it exists so you can tell at a glance whether your own inputs are on the same scale.

faq.q: Is the Metabolic syndrome calculator free to use?
faq.a: Yes — no account, no sign-up and no limit on how many times you run it. The arithmetic happens in your browser, so the values you type are not sent anywhere.
